correctness.rationale: The norm-convergent Abel formula T(z)=Σ(a_n−a_{n+1})P_n is analytic on Re z>0 and uniformly sector bounded. The decomposition is strongly dense; uniform bounds prove C0 continuity. On the real ray I−T(t) is a positive convex combination of I and I−P_n; splitting at N proves limsup upper bound. Superlacunary t_n=(λ_nλ_{n+1})^(−1/2) yields explicit ||T(t_n)−P_n||≤2K(sqrt(λ_n/λ_{n+1})+exp(−sqrt(λ_{n+1}/λ_n))), so the limsup reverse bound follows. In c0-summed 2×2 blocks with u=(1,α),v=(0,1), the exact matrix [[a,0],[α(a−d),d]] has nonnegative rows bounded by a, giving positive contraction ||T(t)||=e^(−4t). Its defect norm sup_j[1−d_j+α(a_j−d_j)] has gap limits 1+α and 1. Positive-time norm-continuity fills exactly [1,1+α]. Finite dimensional blocks yield compact positive-time operators. Edge α=0 and α=1 included.
residual_risks: The equality relies on a spectral superlacunarity condition; not asserted for arbitrary increasing λ.
Finite gap checks supplement but do not establish infinite conclusions.
